sections.title: Lesson 06: Training, adaptation, and data pipelines

keyTerms.definition: Unit 06 of CS229S, covering training, adaptation, and data pipelines.
The evidence label on every lesson claim, here PLANNED with source attribution pending.

recall.question: What unit and sessions anchor this lesson?
recall.answer: Unit cs229s-U06, concepts C01 to C12, calendar-anchored to Oct 18 (Adapting LLMs), Oct 21, Oct 25 (Data in AI Pipelines), and the Oct 23 Dettmers guest talk.

keyTerms.definition: The fixed structure every concept carries, from source and scope to visual units.
Scaling-law and pipeline numbers computed here, not vendor claims.

recall.question: What are the shared bridges for this lesson?
recall.answer: P10 (ML foundations and evaluation), P11 (neural networks and autodiff), P14 (transformer mechanics), P17 (reinforcement learning).

keyTerms.definition: Loss is a straight line on log-log paper, with a floor.
Test loss at parameter count N.
Architecture, data mix, and optimizer recipe: change any and the line moves.

recall.question: Write the two-point fit formulas.
recall.answer: Slope b = (log10 L2 - log10 L1) / (log10 N2 - log10 N1). Intercept a = log10 L1 - b * log10 N1.

recall.question: N1=1e9 L1=2.40, N2=1e10 L2=2.02. Fit and predict N=1e11.
recall.answer: b = -0.0748 per decade, a = 1.0534. Predicted L3 = 1.70.

recall.question: The big run beats the prediction by 0.2 loss. Name two causes.
recall.answer: The data mix improved (intercept shift), or the recipe changed. Keep N fixed and double data quality: loss drops while the parameter-only law says it cannot.

keyTerms.definition: The prompt: examples set the format and decision rule in context, weights frozen.
Number of in-context examples.
The curve flattens when the pattern is fully specified.

recall.question: Define k-shot with no weight update.
recall.answer: No gradient flows: P(y | prompt with k examples) concentrates on the demonstrated pattern as k grows.

recall.question: Accuracies 0.52, 0.61, 0.68, 0.71 at k = 0, 1, 5, 10. Deltas?
recall.answer: 0.09, 0.07, 0.03: shrinking deltas, the curve saturates.

recall.question: A(50) < A(10). Name the cause.
recall.answer: Noisy examples: the context fills with contradictions and the format signal dilutes.

keyTerms.definition: A step function on top of a ramp looks like a cliff: the jump is in the measurement.
The continuous underlying skill, smooth in log N.

recall.question: Define the threshold artifact.
recall.answer: A discontinuous reported metric M(N) = 1[s(N) > t] on a smooth ramp s(N): the jump is in the measurement, not the mind.

recall.question: s(N) = 0.05*log10(N) + 0.1, threshold 0.7. Find N* and the continuous gap from 1e9 to 1e12.
recall.answer: N* = 1e12. Continuous scores 0.55 to 0.70: gap 0.15 while the metric jumps 1.0.

recall.question: A benchmark jumps 40 points at one scale. What do you check first?
recall.answer: Whether the metric is a threshold on a smooth underlying score: replace the 0/1 metric with the continuous score and replot.

keyTerms.definition: SFT on instruction-response pairs: imitation with a mask.
The whole trick: instruction tokens carry zero loss weight.

recall.question: Write the masked SFT loss.
recall.answer: Loss = -mean over response tokens of log P(y_t | x, y_<t).

recall.question: Response log-probs sum to -4.3 over 12 tokens. Loss and response perplexity?
recall.answer: Loss = 0.358. Perplexity = e^0.358 = 1.43.

recall.question: The model echoes instructions instead of answering. What leaked?
recall.answer: The mask: instruction tokens counted in the loss teach the model to predict instructions.

keyTerms.definition: The KL to the SFT model: no leash, the policy games the reward.
P(A beats B) = sigmoid(r_A - r_B).
The policy finds high-scoring, unhelpful answers.

recall.question: Write the Bradley-Terry formula and the KL-regularized objective.
recall.answer: P(A beats B) = sigmoid(r_A - r_B). RL objective: E[r] - beta * KL(policy || SFT).

recall.question: r_A=1.2, r_B=0.8, KL=2.5, beta=0.1. Compute P(A wins) and the objective.
recall.answer: P(A wins) = sigmoid(0.4) = 0.5987. Objective = 1.0 - 0.25 = 0.75.

recall.question: Reward climbs, human ratings fall. Name the failure.
recall.answer: Reward hacking.

keyTerms.definition: The constitution: principles in prose the model grades itself against.
sum_i w_i * s_i(y): principle weights summing to 1.
The classic unstated bias: the judge rewards long, confident-sounding answers.

recall.question: Define the critique-revise loop.
recall.answer: The model reads its draft, critiques it per principle, rewrites it; the pair (revised beats original) trains the reward model.

recall.question: Weights (0.6, 0.4), scores (0.9, 0.5), revision lifts helpful to 0.8. Scores and margin?
recall.answer: Original 0.74, revised 0.86, margin 0.12.

recall.question: Revisions get longer but not better. What is missing?
recall.answer: A verbosity principle: the constitution says nothing about length, so the judge's bias flows into the policy.

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: freeze the giant, train a thin rank-r detour B A.
The frozen (d, k) weight; at inference, fold the hallway in: W = W0 + B A.

recall.question: Write the LoRA update and the param count.
recall.answer: W = W0 + B A. Trainable params: r * (d + k) vs full d * k.

recall.question: d=k=4096, r=16. LoRA params, full params, ratio?
Loss stalls at rank 8 but full fine-tuning works. Name the cause.
recall.answer: Rank r is insufficient: the task needs a move the low-rank subspace cannot carry.

keyTerms.definition: Training: fetch, decode, batch, compute. The line runs at the slowest station.
Per-step compute time: the line speed when compute-bound.
The next bottleneck when workers exceed disk concurrency.

recall.question: Write the overlapped step-time formula.
recall.answer: Step time = max(t_compute, t_fetch + t_assemble) when fully overlapped.

recall.question: Compute 2.0 s, fetch 0.5 s, assemble 0.3 s; slow disk fetch 2.5 s; then doubled workers. Step time and utilization?
recall.answer: Fast: 2.0 s, 100%. Slow disk: 2.8 s, 71%. Doubled workers: 2.0 s, 100%.

recall.question: 32 workers, no speedup. Name the likely bottleneck.
recall.answer: The metadata server or disk concurrency: fetch stops falling and jitter rises.

keyTerms.definition: Preprocessing: each stage keeps a fraction, token yield is the product.
q1, q2, ... per stage: yield = product of q_i.
Dedup needs a hash table of the corpus: MinHash or exact.

recall.question: Write the yield formula.
recall.answer: Yield = product of keep rates. Tokens out = tokens in * yield.

recall.question: 1000 docs, 500 tokens each, keep 0.85 then 0.80. Yield and tokens? Then q2 = 0.5?
recall.answer: Yield 0.68, 340,000 tokens. With q2 = 0.5: yield 0.425, 212,500 tokens.

recall.question: Math scores drop after filtering. What did the filter do?
recall.answer: The aggressive quality filter dropped code and math (odd punctuation): it kept what it could score.

keyTerms.definition: Concatenate short sequences into full bins instead of padding to the longest.
Blocks cross-document attention inside a bin: packing corrupts training without it.

recall.question: Define packing and the document mask.
recall.answer: Packing concatenates short sequences into full bins. The document mask stops attention leaking across documents.

recall.question: Lengths [800,600,400,300,200,100], bin 1024. Naive vs packed efficiency and pad counts?
recall.answer: Naive: 50%, 2400 pad tokens. Packed: 78%, 672 pad tokens (3.6x fewer).

recall.question: Eval looks fine but long documents ramble. What broke?
recall.answer: The document mask: a bug lets tokens attend across documents, and eval perplexity misses the coherence break.

keyTerms.definition: Throughput: tokens per second = batch * length / step time.
Throughput: B * T / t_step tokens/s.
Tokens to a target loss: the metric for recipe choices.

recall.question: Write the throughput formula.
recall.answer: R = B * T / t_step (tokens/s).

recall.question: Batch 32, seq 512, step 2.0 s, toy price $24/hour. R and cost per million? With packing lift?
recall.answer: R = 8192 tok/s, $0.81 per million tokens. Packing lifts real tokens 1.56x: 12,779 tok/s, $0.52 per million.

recall.question: R rises but loss stalls. What is wrong with the metric?
recall.answer: All tokens are not equal: pad tokens taught nothing. Time-to-loss improves only on real tokens.

keyTerms.definition: One run is an anecdote. A seed sweep is evidence.
s over n seeds: the spread a recipe gap must clear.
Atomic adds make the same seed give different losses: spread measures kernel noise.

recall.question: Define the seed-sweep protocol.
recall.answer: Fix code and data order per seed, vary only the seed, report mean plus spread.

recall.question: Losses [2.31, 2.29, 2.33, 2.30, 2.32]. Mean, std, tie call vs recipe B at 2.295?
recall.answer: Mean 2.31, std 0.0158. Gap 0.015 is under 1 std: call it a tie, keep the simpler recipe.

recall.question: Same seed, different loss on rerun. Name two causes.
recall.answer: Nondeterministic GPU kernels (atomic adds), or unseeded data ordering.

keyTerms.definition: pretrain -> SFT (masked) -> preference (RLHF/RLAIF) -> LoRA patch, data pipeline feeding every stage.
Feeds every adaptation stage.

recall.question: What is the U06 chapter plate?
recall.answer: The adaptation ladder: pretrain to SFT (masked) to preference (RLHF/RLAIF) to LoRA patch, with the data pipeline feeding every stage.

Replicate the scaling-law fit on three toy scales; test whether a threshold metric manufactures an emergence jump.

recall.question: What does this unit propose?
recall.answer: Replicate the scaling-law fit on three toy model scales, then test whether a threshold metric manufactures an emergence jump on a synthetic task. See lab-06.
